Right to land and shelter
*61. SHRI RA VULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
HOUSING AND URBAN POVERTY
ALLEVIATION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any
proposal to provide shelter to the poor
and landless people by enacting a law like
right to land and right to shelter;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor;
(d) whether it is a fact that poor people
are agitating for land in Andhra Pradesh;
(e) if so, the details thereof;
(f) whether some people have died due
to police action during the recent agitation;
(g) if so, the details thereof; and
(h) the steps Government are taking to
give land and house to the weaker and
poorer sections of the society, especially
in Andhra Pradesh?
New rules for protection of wild tigers
*62. SHRI R. SHUNMUGA-
SUNDARAM: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made any
request to China for lifting the ban on
trading in tiger parts;
(b) if so, the steps which are being taken
to protect wild tiger from depletion;
(c) whether any attempt has been made
to amend the existing rules in this regard;
and
(d) whether there is a proposal to frame
new rules?
Venue crunch for wedding ceremonies
*63. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of URBAN
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the Capital city is reeling under severe

20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
venue crunch during peak wedding season;
(b) whether Government are also aware
that people have started organising
weddings on roads which is causing trouble
to residents in that area;
(c) whether Government propose to
appeal to the High Court to lift ban on
farm houses and banquet halls to solemnise
marriages; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Freight rates in the country
†*64. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that freight rates
in India are higher in comparison to the
freight rates of international level;
(b) if so, the facts in this regard;
(c) the average difference between these
freight rates; and
(d) the main reasons therefor?
Missing of blank passport booklets
*65. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will
the Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether thousands of blank passport
booklets and visa stickers were found
missing from Missions and posts abroad
and if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether a well-oiled racket,
involving the local police and passport
offices issuing fake passports to foreign
nationals from Afghanistan, Bangladesh,
Pakistan and Sri Lanka exists;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the corrective measures taken to
check malpractices and deficiencies in
passport offices; and
(e) the action taken against the officials
responsible for issuing fake passports to
foreign nationals and for loss of blank
passport booklets and visa stickers?
Nuclear agreement with America
†*66. SHRI PYARELAL
KHANDELWAL: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL  AFF AIRS be pleased to
state:
(a) the latest position of the bilateral
nuclear agreement (123 Agreement) signed
between India and America;
(b) the issues over which differences
have developed between the two countries
in the implementation of the said
Agreement;
(c) whether any discussion was held on
this issue with America during the recent
visit of the Prime Minister to Germany for
attending the G-8 Conference there;
(d) the number of rounds of discussions
held so far between the two countries in
order to resolve the said differences of
opinion; and
(e) the details of the outcome of the
discussions held?
Cost overruns due to delay in Central
projects
*67. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of STATISTICS AND
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether cost overruns amounting to
Rs. 48483.68 crores have been recorded in
respect of the total number of 742 Central

21
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
schemes that were delayed until March,
2006, while multi-State projects have
emerged as the most problematic to
implement;
(b) whether as per 250th flash report of
the Union Ministry for Central sector
projects, only four projects out of 475
under implementation are ahead of the
original schedule and 58 mega projects of
Rs. 1,000 crore and 338 medium schemes
(Rs. 20 crore-100 crore) are on the delayed
list effective March, 2006; and
(c) the steps Government propose to
reduce delay in all the projects?
Fiscal incentives for housing sector
*68. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA:
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of HOUSING AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) the fiscal incentives given to the
housing sector in the country;
(b) whether Government give special
incentives for the housing for economically
weaker sections;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether Government agree with the
findings of the recent report of the National
Building Organisation that most of the
incentives are being cornered by high-
income groups; and
(e)  the steps that are being taken  by
Government for the equitable distribution
of the benefits of such incentives?
Integrated Forest Protection Scheme
(IFPS)
†*69. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) the prescribed norms for providing
grants to various States under the Integrated
Forest Protection Scheme (IFPS);
(b) whether it is a fact that the grant is
not provided to various States on the basis
of their forest areas;
(c) whether it is being considered to
allocate grant on the basis of forest area
under the Integrated Forest Protection
Scheme; and
(d) if  so, by when this process is likely
to be implemented?
Resolution of Kashmir problem
*70. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether his Ministry has received a
proposal from the President of Pakistan,
seeking resolution of the so-called "Kashmir
problem" and affirmed to the media
subsequently to be open to "new ideas" to
resolve the "Kashmir issue";
(b) if so, the details of the "Kashmir
problem" perceived, if any, by the Pakistani
President in his proposal and/or that of the
"Kashmir issue" as hinted to the media by
the Indian Prime Minister;
(c) whether it is a fact that discussions/
negotiations are being conducted at the
official level between the two countries;
(d) if so, the objective thereof; and
(e) the road-map to achieve the same?
Indians in foreign jails
*71. SHRI P.R. RAJAN: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of citizens and service

22
personnel who are in the jails of our
neighbouring countries;
(b) whether it is a fact that a lot of
innocent people, including fishermen, are
jailed in those countries; and
(c) whether Government have initiated
any steps to get them released?
Construction of road in non-
demarcated Indian territory
†*72. SHRI SATYAVRAT
CHATURVEDI:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of EXTERNAL
AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether a road is being constructed
by China in non-demarcated Indian
territory;
(b) whether the construction of a
metalled road upto the Everest Base Camp
at a cost of dollar 2 crore is a matter of
concern from the security point of view;
(c) whether Minister of Cultural Affairs
of China, Mr. Sun Jia Jang who visited India
recently had confirmed that construction
work on the 108 km. long highway would
continue;
(d) whether this construction would
destroy the age old ecology of Himalayas;
and
(e) whether Government have raised the
issue of road construction with the
Government of China?
Urban poor
*73. SHRIMATI PREMA CARIAPPA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
 Will the Minister of HOUSING AND
URBAN POVERTY ALLEVIATION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether an independent study by
an NGO 'Urban Health Resource Centre'
has found that nearly 30 per cent or 90
million people living in urban areas are poor
and according to UN Habitat, the number
is likely to touch 200 million in 2020;
(b) whether the study that has analysed
data collected by the National Family Health
Survey-II points out that development
indices such as infant mortality and
maternal health are also low in urban areas;
(c) if so, the other main features of the
report; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
take in this regard?
Survey and report on educational
status of Muslims
†*74. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of STATISTICS AND
PROGRAMME IMPLEMENTATION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry
of Minority Affairs had requested for
conducting a separate survey and
preparation of a report by NSSO on
educational status of Muslims;
(b) if so, when such request was made
by that Ministry;
(c) whether follow-up action has also
been taken after accepting the request; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Enhancement of spectrum availability
*75. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Telecom Regulatory
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

23
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Authority of India has proposed to cap
the number of telecom operators, prompted
by the unavailability of spectrum;
(b) whether Government consider that
such a move by TRAI would curtail
competition in the telecom industry to the
detriment of consumers; and
(c) the steps being taken to enhance
spectrum availability to accommodate new
players in the industry?
Silt along Ganga at Allahabad
*76. SHRIMATI  JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that River Ganga
at Allahabad has been depositing heavy silt
along the bank on Allahabad side;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
main channel has swung away towards the
low lands on Phaphamau side;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the main
channel, as a result of tangential flow
towards the left bank, is liable to cause
colossal loss of property, cut off rail and
road communication from across Ganga and
cause long term damage; and
(d) if so, the steps Government have
taken to address the situation?
Indo-China visa regime
*77. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of EXTERNAL AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to liberalize
Indo-China visa regime to enhance strategic
cooperation;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether both the countries propose
to work out a number of initiatives to boost
tourism between the two countries; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Indians detected in Pakistani jails
*78. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of
EXTERNAL  AFF AIRS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether a number of Indians visited
Pakistan early this year and were allowed
by Pakistan Government to visit certain
jails in that country in search of their kin
who were expected to have been languishing
in Pak jails after 1965 and 1971 wars or
otherwise strayed into that country
without proper documents;
(b) if so, the number of Indians detected
in Pakistani jails; and
(c) the action taken so far by Indian
Government for their release and
repatriation?
Pruning of Centrally sponsored
schemes
*79. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the Planning Commission's
move to drastically prune Centrally
sponsored schemes from 155 to just 24
and transfer of a bulk of the schemes to
States has not been approved by
Government;
(b) whether Planning Commission has
decided to take a comprehensive look into
all the 300-plus Centrally sponsored
schemes and see that some non-performing
ones could be weeded out and some other
merged with similar schemes to address the
issue of funds for the social sector
programmes; and

24
(c) whether Commission has taken a
decision to provide funds to all the schemes
during the Eleventh Plan period?
IT enabled office administration
*80. SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY  be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of Government's
guidelines to earmark certain percentage of
planned allocations to the Ministries to
enhance usage of IT in the administration;
(b) whether such guidelines would also
include training the personnel into IT-
enabled office administration;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor, and
whether Government would consider
including the training in IT into the existing
guidelines;
(d) whether it is a fact that certain
Ministries/Departments have been using
such funds for the procurement of office
hardware other than computer and related
hardware; and
(e) if so, the mechanism to monitor the
proper usage of such earmarked funds?

Total number of questions — 148

Reprocessing of atomic fuel
441. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether India has made a fresh
proposal by offering to set up a dedicated
safeguarding facility for reprocessing of
atomic fuel before the US;
(b) whether this issue has been
discussed by the Prime Minister and the
US President, who met recently; and
(c) if so, the outcome of the proposal?
Building of new heavy water reactors
442. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to build eight
new heavy water reactors of 700 MW each
in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof, indicating
those that are proposed to be located in
Orissa; and
(c) the details of additional power
production that would be generated as a
result thereof?
Total reserves of thorium
†443. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI BALAVANT ALIAS BAL
APTE:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the experiments carried out in the
direction of producing atomic energy from
thorium and the possibilities thereof;
(b) the names of the States and the
number of reserves found therein;
(c) whether it is also available in the sea
between India and Sri Lanka;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

103
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(d) the efforts being made to preserve
and utilize them; and
(e) the percentage of atomic energy that
could be met out of the total available
reserves of thorium?
Crisis of nuclear scientists in the
country
†444. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Multinational
companies associated with the production
of nuclear energy are becoming active in
the country;
(b) whether it is also a fact that these
companies are offering employment to the
excellent scientists of the country with
attractive pay and perks and as a result, of
which there is a crisis of nuclear scientists
in the country;
(c) whether Government are formulating
any scheme in this regard;
(d) whether Multinational companies
in the field of nuclear energy would affect
country’s security in any way; and
(e) if so, whether Government have
formulated any scheme in this regard?
Spillage of radioactive material of
Narsannapeta
445. SHRI C. RAMA-
CHANDRAIAH: Will the PRIME
MINISTER be pleased to state:
(a) whether the trailer carrying the radio
active yellow cake have overturned at
Narsannapeta in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) if so, whether any spillage of radio
active material and the subsequent
environmental contamination have been
noticed by the authorities;
(c) whether any directions have been
given to the authorities to take measures
which can prevent occurrence of such
accidents;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Revival of MAMC, Durgapur
446. SHRI TAPAN KUMAR SEN:
SHRI MOHAMMED AMIN:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether an MoU has been signed
between the Coal India Limited and DVC
to examine prospects for revival of Mining
and Allied Machinery Corporation
(MAMC), Durgapur;
(b) if so, the features of the MoU; and
(c) the tentative time expected to be
taken for a decision in principle to revive
the MAMC?
Production of coal by private sector
†447. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have finalized identification of the coalfields
where production of coal has been decided
to be assigned to the private sector;
(b) if so, the total number of such
coalfields till June, 2007;
(c) the number of coalfields wherein

104
mining work has been assigned to private
sector during the year 2007, so far; and
(d) the number of mines which are likely
to be assigned to private sector during
residual period of the year?
Increase in royalty rate of coal
†448. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the royalty rate of coal has
been increased;
(b) the details of the royalty which coal
producing States are getting; and
(c) whether it is based on market price
of the coal according to the demands made
by the States?
Loss of stamp and registration fees
†449. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that State
Governments are losing stamp and
registration fees due to absence of any
contract between the coal companies and
State Governments;
(b) whether the need to constitute a
separate forum is being felt for better
coordination between the Central and State
Governments to solve the problems
connected with coal; and
(c) if so, the efforts being made by
Government in this regard?
Increase in cyber crimes
450. SHRI TARIQ ANW AR: Will the
Minister of  COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the number
of cyber crimes has been increasing in the
country during the last three years;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps Government would take
in this regard?
Growth rate of mobile phones
451. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the subscribers base for mobile
phones in the country;
(b) the annual growth rate of mobile
phones in India for the years 2003-04 to
2006-07;
(c) the number of subscriber lines which
were added by BSNL and MTNL during
the last three years, year-wise; and
(d) the share of business between Public
Sector and Private Sector?
Redressal of complaints regarding
poor telecom services
452. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: W ill the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
complaints regarding disappointing telecom
services;
(b) if so, the number of complaints
received till date, during the last three years
and the number of complaints redressed so
far out of them, State-wise; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

105
(c) the action taken by Government
after conducting the inquiry in this regard?
Opening of new post offices
453. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether a number of villages in the
country are without post office;
(b) if so, the number of villages that are
not having post office, State-wise and
category-wise, till date;
(c) the steps taken to meet the
requirement of people for post office in
these villages;
(d) whether there is any proposal to
open post offices in private sector;
(e) if so, the details including the number
of such post offices opened/proposed to
be opened in private sector, category-wise,
till date; and
(f) whether steps would be taken to
drop the proposal to open post offices in
private sector?
Growth rate of BSNL
†454. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the increase
in the number of subscribers of the cellular
service provided by Bharat Sanchar Nigam
Limited (BSNL) is not increasing in
comparison to private sector companies;
(b) if so, the monthly growth rate of
public sector company during past months
in the year 2006 and 2007 in this regard;
(c) the growth rate of private sector
companies during the said period; and
(d) the assessment regarding financial
loss to the public sector company due to
the said decline?
Postal small savings deposits
455. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL:
SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there has
been a drop in the mobilization of postal
small savings deposits recently due to
higher rate of interest being offered by
banks for deposits;
(b) if so, the details of the deposit
mobilization and withdrawals during the
years 2005-06, 2006-07 and 2007-08 so
far; and
(c) Government’s reaction thereto?
Mobile network expansion project
456. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL:
SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there has been inordinate
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

106
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
delay in execution of BSNL’s mobile
network expansion project; and
(b) if so, the details of the project with
current status and the reasons for delay in
its execution?
Fund allocation for Commonwealth
Games
†457. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
Will the Minister of YOUTH
AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to
state:
(a) the amount allocated by Government
for preparation of Commonwealth Games
to be held in 2010; and
(b) the amount allocated to develop
infrastructure with regard to
accommodation for foreign nationals who
would be visiting India?
CoE of GSM and CDMA operators
458. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that GSM
operators are not using the scare spectrum
efficiently;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and the
action taken by Government against GSM
operators; and
(c) the latest Calculation of Efficiency
(CoE) of GSM and CDMA operators
derived on the basis of subscribers and
MHz?
Upgradation of postal network
459. SHRI DARA SINGH: Will the
Minister of  COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Indian Postal
Department strongly needs to enhance its
technology to compete with the private
players;
(b) if so, the details/proposals put
forward by the Department of Posts to
Government;
(c) whether the Planning Commission
has so far considered any proposals for
inclusion in the Eleventh Five Year Plan in
this regard; and
(d) if so, the likely amount of investment
required for technology upgradation for
postal network with details thereof?
Requirement of spectrum for mobile
services
†460. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Department
of Telecommunications requires 42.5
mega hertz spectrum for mobile services;
(b) by when this additional spectrum is
likely to be obtained; and
(c) whether defence services would be

107
affected by giving additional spectrum to
telecommunication services?
Bidding process for availing subsidy
461. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of telecom companies that
emerged successful in the bidding process
for availing the subsidy proposed to be
extended by Government;
(b) the areas specified for creating
infrastructure in the country as a whole
and Andhra Pradesh in particular;
(c) whether the subsidy being extended
is limited to rural areas only; and
(d) if so, whether it would create dual
rate policy to the subscribers of rural and
urban areas by the service providers?
Consumers of BSNL mobile phones
462. SHRI TARIQ ANW AR: Will the
Minister of COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that consumers
of BSNL mobile phones of bordering
districts of Bihar have to pay roaming
charges as the capacity of towers of West
Bengal are more powerful than of Bihar;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the steps Government would take
to safeguard the interest of consumers?
Supply of cellular equipment for
BSNL
463. DR. M.A.M. RAMASWAMY:
Will the Minister of
COMMUNICATIONS AND
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the tendering process for
